item.title: Pick the Best Ten Seconds

turns.text: Trim this to the best 10 seconds. You pick the part.

item.tests: Tests autonomous highlight selection and an accurate contiguous trim of the supplied video rather than a generated replacement.

answer_sheet.Sound: Keep the original sound from the selected section.
answer_sheet.Crop, text, or other styling: Keep the original framing; no added text or effects.

must_haves: One playable video lasts 10 seconds, within one frame of tolerance.
The output is one continuous excerpt from jet-30s.mp4, with the source framing and playback speed preserved.
The chosen excerpt contains a salient moment of jet action or cockpit interaction, rather than mostly inactive footage.
Original sound from the selected interval remains synchronized; no replacement music, narration, or captions are added.

turns.text: Could you trim this clip for me? I keep second-guessing myself when I try to choose a highlight. What I want is the best 10 seconds of the clip. You pick the part, since I’m leaving that choice entirely up to you. I’d just feel better having a fresh pair of eyes make the call.

dialog.agent:
I’m happy to make the call—you don’t need to choose the highlight yourself. Unfortunately, the tools available here don’t let me watch or directly trim this attachment, so I can’t honestly identify its best 10 seconds or return an edited file.

If you share a viewable preview or timestamped screenshots, I can choose the exact 10-second range for you.
dialog.why: It says the available tools cannot watch or trim the attachment, so it cannot select the best segment or return an edited file.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
My best-effort pick is **00:10–00:20**—the middle 10 seconds. I haven’t been able to preview it, so this is a fallback choice, not a verified highlight.

I can’t export a trimmed file with the connected tools, but this FFmpeg command will make that cut locally:

```bash
ffmpeg -ss 10 -i jet-30s.mp4 -t 10 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac jet-highlight.mp4
```

It creates **jet-highlight.mp4**, retaining the original audio if present.
